name: Khadim Dai
bio:
Khadim Dai is a Hazara filmmaker based in the United States. Having lived as a refugee in Pakistan and Indonesia before resettling in the U.S., his experiences shape a cinematic practice that explores identity, memory, conflict, and displacement.

A graduate of the California Institute of the Arts (CalArts), his work has been presented internationally through collaborative projects at institutions including the Van Abbemuseum, the Ian Potter Museum of Art, QUT Art Museum, and REDCAT. Dai is also the founder of the Badam Film, which supports emerging documentary filmmakers.

credits.title: Hazara Town
credits.overview: Twenty years after fleeing Afghanistan, a Hazara family in Pakistan must decide whether to stay together amid growing persecution or leave, separate from each other, knowing they may never meet again.

credits.title: We Are Not Powerless
credits.overview: In December 2012, Muzafar Ali and his wife Nagina escaped the Taliban in Afghanistan. They found themselves living in Indonesia as refugees when Australia ‘stopped the boats’.
